audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Graves, Skill, Gragas, Gragas, Graves, Gragas, Gragas while the page's own whys give Level 3 to Graves ('he still has no all-in combo to answer it'), call 4-5 a brawl that cancels out, hand Level 6 to Gragas ('Gragas spikes hardest at 6') and say you reclaim the late game.
audit.why: The mirror audit (gragas vs graves) already flipped its chart and its notes state the intended result exactly: Graves ahead at 1 and 3, even at 2 and 4-5, Gragas ahead at 6 and first item, even at 2+ items. Packet levelChart agrees.
audit.corrected: Chart flipped as one atomic group to Graves, Skill, Graves, Skill, Gragas, Gragas, Skill with matching ratings and four rewritten phase whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4] credited Level 6 to Graves' Collateral Damage when Level 6 is Gragas' hardest spike — Explosive Cask (100/85/70s) off a Body Slam engage, with Drunken Rage's damage reduction on a 5s cooldown eating the committed burst.
audit.why: Both ults are similar cooldowns, but his converts an engage into a displacement under turret; yours does not answer that.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names Body Slam into Explosive Cask and Drunken Rage's damage reduction. Body Slam's real 14s rank-1 cooldown written into the do's as the commit trigger.

audit.whatIsWrong: Smoke Screen was called a blind in three places (late, spikes[3], report[10]). Riot's text gives reduced sight range plus impact magic damage and a brief slow — no blind, so his autos and his empowered Drunken Rage attack still land.
audit.why: The advice 'Smoke Screen blinds his autos in 2v2s' tells you to stand and trade inside the cloud, which loses the trade.
audit.corrected: All three restated as sight-cut plus slow, keeping the genuine value: he cannot see your engage and mis-aims the cask.

audit.why: All three packet suspectNames (Drunken Rage x2, Barrel Roll) are false positives — both are Gragas' real ability names.

edits.before: Full kit: Q's wall-bounce return is your real damage — fight near terrain so both hits connect.
edits.after: Full kit at 3: Q into terrain behind him detonates back over him, and he has no all-in to answer.

edits.before: Trade in shell rhythm: two autos and out. Track Body Slam; your armor stacks from E make his short trades unprofitable.
edits.after: Short two-shot brawl: True Grit stacks and his Barrel Roll poke cancel out. Body Slam is 14s — step in once it is spent.

edits.before: Collateral Damage adds an execute and a disengage knockback in one — hold it for either, never for chip.
edits.after: Six is his: Body Slam into Explosive Cask flings you under turret, and Drunken Rage soaks the committed burst.

edits.before: You out-skirmish but the crit scalers pass you — convert to picks with smoke-screen blinds and R snipes.
edits.after: Even at two items — you skirmish better, but stop forcing 1v1s into a Drunken Rage and play for picks.

edits.before: His engage and his escape in one button — punish the cooldown hard. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Body Slam is 14s at rank 1 and it is both his engage and his escape — step in the moment he spends it.

edits.before: You reclaim it as the better skirmisher: weave Quickdraw through the brawl, Smoke Screen his autos and vision in 2v2s, and R-snipe his low-HP recalls across walls.
edits.after: You skirmish better: weave Quickdraw through the brawl, Smoke Screen to cut his sight and slow him in 2v2s — it never blinds — then R-snipe his low-HP recalls across walls.

edits.before: Late, the lane swings back to you because you're the better skirmisher and roamer. In extended brawls your Quickdraw charges and True Grit stacks compound while he's stuck cooldown-to-cooldown, and Smoke Screen blinds his autos and shreds his vision in any 2v2. Stop forcing 1v1s into a Drunken-Rage Gragas and use your mobility instead: collapse on skirmishes, Smoke Screen incoming ganks, and R-snipe his low-HP recalls across walls. Close the game before front-to-back teamfights make his displacement matter more than your DPS.
edits.after: Late, the lane swings back toward you because you're the better skirmisher and roamer. In extended brawls your Quickdraw charges and True Grit stacks compound while he's stuck cooldown-to-cooldown, and Smoke Screen cuts his sight and slows on impact — it never blinds, so he still hits you inside it. Stop forcing 1v1s into a Drunken-Rage Gragas and use mobility instead: collapse on skirmishes, fog incoming ganks, and R-snipe his low-HP recalls across walls. Close before front-to-back fights make his displacement matter more than your DPS.

edits.before: Your W smoke blinds tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.
edits.after: Smoke Screen cuts sight and slows on impact — no blind. Drop it as the gank arrives and fight them blind-sided in the fog.

notes: Chart flipped to the result the already-written mirror (gragas__graves) states, which also matches packet.levelChart: Graves at 1 and 3, even at 2 and 4-5, Gragas at 6 and first item, even at 2+. Smoke Screen blind claims removed from late, spikes[3] and report[10]. All three packet suspectNames are false positives.
